summary: A structurally honest but visually thin Phase 1. The chassis silhouette, red/dark-inset palette, 54/46 deck-keybed split, and a full 73-key E-E keybed (43 white / 30 black, correct black-key pattern and 61% height) are all in place, and a real dual-oscillator additive piano voice (triangle + sine overtone, velocity-scaled AD envelope) is truthfully declared as synthesis in IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json with no recorded-sample claims. The honesty boundary is clean: every panel control is a presentation-only range/switch/button that only mutates a normalized presentation-state map, the two OLEDs (Program + Synth only) show static 'Init Program'/'Init Synth' with no fabricated feature reporting, and a test verifies toggling an Organ switch leaves 'Piano: ready' unchanged. The note lifecycle is complete and well-factored across injectable audio/MIDI/timing boundaries: pointer/multitouch/computer-key (with repeat suppression via e.repeat and code-keyed held set) / MIDI note+velocity+CC64 sustain, denied/disconnected MIDI ignored, deterministic oldest-voice stealing at a 32-voice cap, sustain latch, and blur/disconnect/unmount all-notes-off cleanup. The dominant weakness is visual fidelity: sections are rendered as a uniform flex-wrap grid of identical dark label-boxes with text captions, which is exactly the 'single undifferentiated control grid' / 'uniform repeated knob matrix' the visual spec lists as forbidden for organ, synth, and effects. There is no drawbar-bank rendering, no LED ladders, no distinct knob/dial industrial forms, and the program dial is a tiny slider. Section widths use the older 13/21/15/9/21/21 fractions (piano too wide, program/synth too narrow) that the current visual spec explicitly corrected as photo-contradicted, though the stage-1 prompt still instructed those values. A second real gap is test depth: the entire Web Audio backend is mocked with no-op oscillator/gain nodes and a MockOfflineAudioContext whose startRendering returns a fixed 440Hz sine regardless of input, so no test proves rendered output differs from silence or that velocity/sustain move the actual signal; the unused measureOutputLevel helper would return a constant under those mocks. Audio behavior is asserted only through voice-count and gain-math checks.

criteria.label: Silhouette, chassis, and geometry
evidence: Continuous red chassis with 54/46 deck/keybed split (VERTICAL_ALLOCATION.deck 0.54, keybed 0.46) applied via flex-basis in instrument.tsx; desktop capture shows one unbroken red body with the keybed as the lower band.
Keybed geometry is accurate: 73 keys, 43 white / 30 black, black keys at 61% height and positioned by white-key offsets (keybed.tsx left calc), matching variants.json blackKeyHeightFraction 0.61.
Desktop width uses min(97vw, calc(97vh * 3.095)) targeting the 3.0951 aspect ratio and 88-97% width band; capture at 1440x900 shows no vertical scroll.

Section-order left-to-right (performance, organ, piano, program, synth, effects) matches the photo, but relative widths use the pre-correction fractions (piano 0.15 vs current spec 0.085, program 0.09 vs 0.125, synth 0.21 vs 0.25), so proportions drift from the photographed deck.

criteria.label: Complete hardware inventory and placement
evidence: All six sections and ~163 stable data-control-id controls are present, and displays are correctly restricted to exactly two (program-oled, synth-oled), satisfying 'Program/Synth as the only primary OLEDs'.

Rendering is a uniform flex-wrap grid of identical dark label-boxes (panel-controls: display flex, flex-wrap wrap in styles.css), which matches the visual spec's forbidden 'single undifferentiated control grid' (effects), 'uniform repeated knob matrix' (synth), and 'generic equal-width control grid' (organ).

Landmarks are logically enumerated but not visually rendered: nine drawbars appear as generic range sliders with no drawbar bank or LED ladders, the program dial is a small slider not a large dial, and knobs are visually indistinguishable from buttons in the desktop capture.
Section header labels ('PERFORMANCE CONTROLS', 'ORGAN', 'PIANO'...) are shown as page-style titles the real panel does not carry, reinforcing a generic-form impression.

criteria.label: Materials, color, typography, and displays
evidence: Reference colors are used from spec: chassis #79232c/#721f29, panel #3c424d, key blacks/whites, and OLED blue-green (--oled-bg / --oled-text) render as dark insets on red with teal OLED text.
Branding 'NORD STAGE 4' is present top-left in the performance area, and white uppercase legends are applied to captions and headers.

Control materials are flat: buttons are plain #2a2a2a rounded rects, faders/knobs are native range inputs with accent-color, LEDs are small dots; there is no dimensional knob/fader/drawbar treatment, so material hierarchy is weak versus the photo.
No page errors and no marketing hero; the light neutral product-study background is used as specified.

criteria.label: Narrow retention
evidence: Narrow capture at 390x844 shows the complete chassis, both OLEDs, and the full keybed with no clipping or horizontal overflow (capture.json narrow has empty consoleMessages/pageErrors).
A max-width:480px media query switches the instrument to width 98vw and aspect 3.095/1.15 and hides panel headers and control captions to prevent clipping while keeping controls inspectable.
Controls remain present and operable at narrow width (still real DOM buttons/sliders), though captions are hidden so state legibility is reduced to LED/position cues only.
Keybed keys stay proportional and full-range at narrow width; the instrument remains a single inspectable unit rather than reflowing or breaking.

criteria.label: Unified playable inputs
evidence: All four input paths funnel through one NoteLifecycle/PianoEngine: pointer (keybed.tsx handlePointerDown with setPointerCapture and y-based velocity), independent multitouch (per-pointerId map, test asserts C4/D4 independent aria-pressed), computer keys, and MIDI.

Computer-key repeat is suppressed at both the OS layer (e.repeat early-return in instrument.ts) and the model layer (computerKeysHeld set keyed by code), with a test proving a second KeyDown does not add a second voice.

MIDI handling parses note-on (vel>0), note-off, note-on-vel-0-as-off, and CC64 sustain; attachMidiHandlers returns a no-op detach for 'disconnected'/'denied' ports and a test confirms those events are ignored.
Focus loss cleanup is wired (window blur -> blurCleanup -> computerKeyCancelAll + allNotesOff) and unmount disposes the lifecycle; tests exercise blur cleanup but rely on mocked audio nodes.

criteria.label: Voice lifecycle and performance
evidence: Engine implements velocity (velocityToGain (v/127)^1.4), attack/decay AD envelope, per-note release, repeated/overlapping same-note handling (releaseVoiceForNote before re-trigger), and a 32-voice cap with deterministic oldest-voice stealing by startedAt.
Sustain latch is correct: noteOff while pedal held moves the note into sustainedNotes and keeps the voice; setSustain(false) releases them, with a test asserting voice count stays 1 then drops to 0.
allNotesOff and dispose release every voice and clear sustain state, and a stealing test with polyphony:2 confirms the active count never exceeds the cap.

Because tests run against no-op mock oscillator/gain nodes, lifecycle correctness is proven only at the voice-bookkeeping level, not on rendered audio (no attack/decay duration or steal audibility is measured).

criteria.label: Basic source and status honesty
evidence: IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json truthfully declares Phase 1 audio as 'honest additive synthesis (triangle + sine overtone oscillators with AD envelope)', sampleSources empty, with a note that recorded sets are Phase 2 scope.

engine.ts backs this claim: real createOscillator triangle + sine-overtone-x2 with velocity-scaled gain envelope into a masterGain(0.35) to destination, i.e. one dependable audible voice, not a buffer presented as a recording.

Status honesty is present: constructor sets 'ready' (or 'error' when forceError), noteOn returns -1 in error, and the surface prints 'Piano: ready/error ... Voices: N'; a fallback status type exists though no asset-failure fallback path is needed in Phase 1.
No false provenance or recording claims anywhere; visual-audit.md and the details file both restate the synthesis-not-samples choice.

criteria.label: Control movement and feedback
evidence: Every control kind is operable and exposes state: buttons toggle aria-pressed, toggles/LEDs are role=switch with aria-checked, faders/drawbars/knobs/wheels/stick/encoder are role=slider range inputs with aria-valuemin/max/now, and displays are role=status.
Keys depress via pointer/keyboard with aria-pressed reflected and is-pressed styling; a test confirms pointer down/up flips aria-pressed and multitouch is independent.
A test iterates every control in CONTROLS and asserts a matching data-control-id exists in the DOM, and clicking a decorative switch flips aria-checked.
Focus-visible outlines are defined for both buttons and range inputs, giving visible keyboard focus; captions provide accessible names though they are hidden below 480px.

criteria.label: Decorative-control boundary
evidence: interactControl only calls setControlValue -> setPresentation (a plain presentation-state map in state/instrument.ts); no control handler touches the PianoEngine, audio graph, or note lifecycle.
OLEDs render fixed 'Init Program' / 'Init Synth' strings from createPresentationState and are never updated by any control, so no display reports unimplemented behavior as working.
A test toggles the Organ B3 switch and asserts aria-checked flips to true while 'Piano: ready' remains, proving controls change presentation only and not audio/system state.
Only keybed note and CC64 sustain reach the engine; the honesty contract 'controls work canonically or visibly do nothing' is satisfied with no fabricated success.

criteria.label: Data structure and tests
evidence: Clean separation and stable IDs: normalized CONTROLS/SECTIONS/KEYBED data model, injectable AudioContextFactory/TimingBoundary/MidiInputPort boundaries, and PianoEngine/NoteLifecycle decoupled from React state.
Feature-matrix.json maps all eleven Phase 1 IDs to non-empty test files covering key-count, layout, inventory, key interaction, decorative controls, accessibility, and the four piano feature IDs.

The entire audio backend is mocked with no-op MockOscillatorNode/MockGainNode and a MockOfflineAudioContext whose startRendering returns a fixed 440Hz sine irrespective of input, so audio tests are pure state/count assertions and never cross a real signal boundary.

measureOutputLevel (a real OfflineAudioContext RMS helper) exists in engine.ts but is imported by no test, and the velocity test asserts only velocityToGain math, so no test proves output differs from silence or that velocity/sustain change rendered audio.

criteria.label: Runtime quality
evidence: Both canonical captures record empty consoleMessages and empty pageErrors at 1440x900 and 390x844 (capture.json), indicating a clean runtime with no thrown errors.
Cleanup is thorough: blur -> allNotesOff, MIDI detach on effect teardown, and a lifecycle dispose on unmount, so voices and listeners return to baseline.
ensureStarted resumes the AudioContext on first key press (gesture-gated), and status is surfaced as 'Piano: ready · Voices: N' in the live status line.

The four package gates (test/typecheck/lint/build) are wired with a committed lockfile and dist/index.html present; runtime stability under repeated interaction is supported by the pointer-capture and per-pointer bookkeeping, though not stress-tested.

issues.detail: Panel sections render as a uniform flex-wrap grid of identical dark label-boxes with no drawbar bank, LED ladders, or distinct knob/dial forms, matching the visual spec's explicitly forbidden 'single undifferentiated control grid' / 'uniform repeated knob matrix' for organ, synth, and effects.

Section widths use the pre-correction fractions (13/21/15/9/21/21) that the current visual spec flags as photo-contradicted (piano too wide, program/synth too narrow); the stage-1 prompt still lists those older values, so the candidate followed its prompt but drifts from the authoritative reference photo.

All audio tests run against no-op mock nodes and a MockOfflineAudioContext returning a fixed sine, so no test proves rendered output differs from silence or that velocity/sustain/release change the actual signal; the real measureOutputLevel helper is unused. Voice behavior is asserted only via counts and gain math.
